questions.q: What is a data custodian primarily responsible for?
options: The safe custody, transport, and storage of data, and implementing the owner and steward's rules
Deciding what counts as 'good enough' quality for a domain
Approving who gets access to a data domain
Writing the company's data governance charter
questions.explain: Custodians implement the technical environment — storage, security, movement — that enforces decisions the owner and steward have already made.

questions.q: Which question does the custodian role answer, as distinct from owner and steward?
options: Where does this data physically live, and who implements the controls?
Who decides what the rules are?
What does this data mean to the business?
Which regulator has jurisdiction over this data?
questions.explain: Owner answers 'who decides,' steward answers 'what does it mean and is it good enough,' and custodian answers the technical 'where does it live and who implements it.'

options: Anyone who uses data to do their job without holding owner, steward, or custodian responsibility for it
Only external customers who purchase a company's data products
A synonym for data custodian
Someone who has no governance responsibilities whatsoever
questions.explain: Consumers are the largest group touching data in most organizations — analysts, managers, reps — and they still carry lighter, real governance responsibilities.

questions.q: Which of these IS a governance responsibility expected of a data consumer?
options: Reporting data that looks wrong instead of quietly working around it
Setting the domain's official quality threshold
Approving another team's access request
Implementing the database's encryption settings
questions.explain: Consumers don't hold formal authority, but they are expected to follow access rules, report problems, respect classification, and give feedback.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat 'steward' and 'custodian' as distinct roles even though DAMA-DMBOK's core text calls them near-synonyms?
options: In practice, understanding what data means and understanding how the systems holding it work are different skill sets usually held by different people
DAMA-DMBOK's definitions have been fully retired and no longer apply
Custodians are always more senior than stewards
The two terms refer to entirely unrelated areas of the business with no connection at all
questions.explain: A steward needs business/subject-matter understanding; a custodian needs technical/platform understanding — distinct enough skills that organizations usually assign them to different people.
